# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_FLAT_TO_EXPANSION_WITH_RSI_PULLBACK

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon flattens (indicating equilibrium) and then begins to expand in the direction of a pullback to the 50‑% RSI level, the ensuing move often captures the next swing. This edge exists because ribbon compression precedes expansion phases in trending markets, and pulling back to the RSI midpoint during expansion provides a high-probability entry point aligned with the emerging momentum.

## Mechanism

Entry rule: If the ribbon width (EMA(55) - EMA(8)) contracts to < 0.05% of price for two consecutive 5‑min bars (flat) AND the next bar shows ribbon expanding (width increase > 0.02%) AND price pulls back to RSI(14) between 40‑60 (for long) or 40‑60 (for short) with a bullish/bearish candle closing > VWAP (long) or < VWAP (short), then enter long/short at the close of that bar. Exit shape: Stop = prior swing low/high before the expansion bar; target = 2× risk or trail using premium‑stop % (15% of ATR) from highest close after entry. Regime hint: Ideal in low‑to‑moderate VIX (15‑25) and during the 10:30‑12:00 ET window when the ribbon tends to transition from consolidation to trend.
